chief_complaint: sudden tearing interscapular back pain, high BP
hpi_details: A 41-year-old male presents to the clinic with sudden tearing interscapular back pain, high bp. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks he severely threw out a back muscle or pinched a nerve between his shoulder blades while shifting heavy furniture.
concerns: He is worried that a ruptured spinal disc or nerve will permanently paralyze him and leave him unable to provide for his family.
expectations: He hopes to get a spinal X-ray and a strong injection of muscle relaxants to walk back out today.

investigation_events.title: CT angiography of the aorta
investigation_events.availability_message: The CT angiography report is now available.

results.value: Acute aortic dissection flap beginning at the aortic root and extending through the ascending aorta into the arch; small hemopericardium without active rupture

clinical_knowledge.topic: Stanford Type A Aortic Dissection evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Stanford Type A Aortic Dissection is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes IV esmolol for heart-rate control (target HR <60) followed by blood-pressure control (target SBP 100-120) in Stanford Type A Dissection, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

Key HPI features: A 41-year-old male presents to the clinic with sudden tearing interscapular back pain, high bp. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Stanford Type A Dissection.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Stanford Type A Aortic Dissection.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Myocardial infarction without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Pulse deficit.
management_principles: Plan for Stanford Type A Dissection: IV Esmolol, target HR <60, SBP 100-120
Emergent CT angiography of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis (or transesophageal echocardiography if unstable), with immediate cardiothoracic surgical consultation
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: A tear in the aortic wall causing sudden tearing back pain and high blood pressure, needing heart-rate control before blood pressure control.

must_ask.say: Do you have high blood pressure?

history.answer: Doctor, I have this sudden, excruciating tearing pain between my shoulder blades, and my blood pressure was dangerously high when they checked it.
It is right between my shoulder blades in my upper back, and it feels like it is tearing downward through my spine toward my chest, not radiating down my legs.
It hit me all of a sudden about two hours ago out of nowhere. I wasn't lifting anything heavy and I didn't fall or hurt myself.
It feels like a sharp, ripping, tearing sensation inside my chest and back. On a scale of one to ten, it's definitely a ten.
Nothing makes it better, neither resting nor changing positions. Deep breathing or coughing makes the chest discomfort slightly worse, but the severe ripping pain stays constant.
Yes, lying down doesn't relieve it at all; the intense pain has been relentless since the moment it started.
No, I have never had morning stiffness in my back or joints, and moving around does not ease this pain.
My legs don't feel numb or weak, though my left arm has felt slightly cool and heavy since the pain started.
No, I have normal feeling around my groin and buttocks, and I haven't lost control of my urine or stool.
history.topic: Saddle anesthesia and bowel bladder control

history.answer: No, I don't get leg cramping or numbness when I walk, and bending forward doesn't change anything.
No fever, no unexpected weight loss, and no night sweats, but I broke into a cold sweat when this pain hit.
history.topic: Fever, weight loss, or night sweats

history.answer: No, I have never had cancer.
No recent infections, no spine injections or back surgeries, no diabetes, and I don't use any intravenous drugs.
No, I don't have osteoporosis, have never taken steroid medications, and haven't had any falls.
I feel a slight ache spreading into my upper abdomen, but I haven't noticed any pulsing sensation in my stomach, nor any urinary problems or blood in my urine.
No red or painful eyes, no heel pain, no chronic diarrhea, and no skin rash or psoriasis.
I took two ibuprofen tablets at home when it started, but they didn't touch the pain at all.
I haven't been diagnosed with high blood pressure before, but I rarely see a doctor so I haven't checked it in years.
Yes, I also feel a severe tightness and tearing feeling in the center of my chest, and it feels hard to catch my breath from the intense pain.
history.topic: Chest pain and shortness of breath

history.answer: I have been feeling quite fatigued and washed out recently, and right now I feel lightheaded and exhausted.
I felt this sudden rip between my shoulder blades and figured I had pinched a nerve or torn a muscle moving furniture.
The pain tore right down my spine, and I am terrified a nerve snapped and I will end up paralyzed.
I just want an X-ray to check my spine and a strong shot for the pain so I can walk back out of here.
I have been healthy overall with no chronic medical conditions.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been hospitalized.
I don't take any regular prescription medications or supplements.
I don't have any known allergies to medications.
I have never smoked cigarettes.
I only drink socially, maybe a beer or glass of wine once or twice a month.
I work an office desk job in finance and live with my wife.
My father had high blood pressure, but no one in my family has had an aneurysm, aortic dissection, or genetic connective tissue disorders.

exam.finding: Patient appears pale, diaphoretic, and in acute distress clutching his chest and upper back.

Blood pressure 185/100 mmHg in right arm and 155/90 mmHg in left arm, heart rate 98 beats per minute, respiratory rate 20 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 98% on room air, temperature 36.6 degrees Celsius.
Tachycardic, regular rhythm, normal S1 and S2; faint early diastolic decrescendo murmur audible along the right upper sternal border; no pericardial friction rub.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally throughout all lung fields without wheezes, rales, or rhonchi.
Right radial and carotid pulses are strong and bounding; left radial pulse is diminished and delayed; bilateral femoral pulses are palpable.
Abdomen is soft, non-distended, without guarding or rebound tenderness; no pulsatile abdominal mass detected.
Normal spinal contour with no midline spinous process or paraspinal muscle tenderness; negative bilateral straight leg raise tests.
Motor strength is 5/5 in all four extremities with symmetric bulk and tone.
Intact light touch and pinprick sensation in all extremities and throughout the perineal saddle area.
